drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. We have incorporated your proposed cash-at-closing structure and thirty-day closing framework for discussion, subject to client approval and agreement on price, share particulars and closing conditions. The draft also develops the proposed representation categories. Your twelve-month survival period, 1% deductible basket, 10% cap and exclusive-remedy provision remain bracketed proposals, not agreed terms. Fundamental representations, actual fraud, indemnity procedures and the scope of undisclosed-liability protection require express agreement before execution. Please provide the Seller and issuer particulars, proposed price, identified financial statements and disclosure schedules.

edits.text: PARTIES. This Agreement is between [Seller legal name, jurisdiction and entity type] as Seller and Meridian Acquisitions LLC, a [jurisdiction] limited liability company, as Buyer. The shares to be purchased are [number and class] shares of [issuer legal name, jurisdiction and entity type], representing [percentage]% of its issued and outstanding share capital (the “Shares”).

1. PURCHASE PRICE. Subject to agreement on the amount, currency and any purchase-price adjustments, Buyer shall purchase the Shares for [currency and amount] (the “Purchase Price”). At Closing, Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price in full by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by Seller in writing, against delivery of the Shares and the agreed closing deliverables. No escrow, holdback, deferred consideration or financing condition shall apply. [Payment structure subject to client approval.]

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur on a mutually agreed date no later than thirty days after signing (the “Outside Date”), subject only to the conditions expressly set out in [agreed closing-conditions schedule], including the specifically identified approvals, consents and deliverables. A condition may be waived only in writing by the party entitled to its benefit, to the extent legally permissible. If Closing has not occurred by the Outside Date, either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice, unless that party’s breach prevented Closing. Termination shall not release liability for any pre-termination breach. The parties may extend the Outside Date by written agreement. [Conditions, deliverables and termination consequences remain subject to agreement.]

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Subject to specifically identified exceptions in agreed disclosure schedules, Seller shall represent as of signing and Closing that: (a) Seller has authority to execute and perform this Agreement and has obtained the necessary authorizations; (b) Seller owns and can transfer good title to the Shares, free of liens other than expressly agreed permitted liens; (c) the issuer’s capitalization, including outstanding shares and rights to acquire shares, is accurately stated in the agreed capitalization schedule; and (d) the financial statements identified in [schedule, including dates] have been prepared in accordance with [agreed accounting standards] and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results for the periods covered, subject to expressly agreed qualifications. [Representation scope, qualifications, disclosure standards and classification of fundamental representations remain subject to agreement.]

4. INDEMNITY. Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses arising from breaches of Seller’s representations and from undisclosed liabilities, in each case within a scope and subject to exclusions and claims procedures expressly agreed by the parties. [Seller proposal—not agreed: general representation and undisclosed-liability claims survive twelve months after Closing, are subject to a deductible basket equal to 1% of the Purchase Price and an aggregate cap equal to 10% of the Purchase Price, exclude matters adequately disclosed under the agreed disclosure standard, and constitute Buyer’s exclusive remedy for those claims.] Buyer shall not recover more than once for the same loss. Fundamental representations and actual fraud shall be addressed separately and shall not be subject to the bracketed limitations unless expressly agreed. [The parties must agree the definition of losses, covered liabilities, survival and timely-notified claim treatment, notice requirements, third-party defense and settlement rights, treatment of covenant claims, and the scope of any exclusive-remedy provision and its exceptions before execution.]
Please supply the proposed price and currency and confirm whether any adjustment mechanism is contemplated. No price or economic acceptance is implied by this draft.

The bracketed survival, basket, cap and exclusive-remedy language records Seller’s proposal only. Please propose separate treatment for fundamental representations and actual fraud, and detailed indemnity procedures. All brackets and outstanding comments must be resolved before execution.

partner.private_reasoning: The rendered agreement and cover note do not disclose the client's confidential severance threshold or imply it. No hidden content is identified in the supplied package. Approval is for transmission of this discussion draft, not acceptance of its proposed terms.

receiver.message_back: Subject to Seller’s approval and confirmation of price, party/share particulars and schedules, we propose full cash payment at Closing without escrow, holdback or financing condition within thirty days, with specifically enumerated closing conditions; general-representation and undisclosed-liability claims would be limited to twelve months, a 1% deductible basket and an aggregate 10% cap, excluding fairly disclosed matters, liabilities reserved in the identified financial statements and ordinary-course liabilities incurred thereafter. Authority, title and capitalization claims would instead survive twenty-four months with an aggregate purchase-price cap, actual fraud by Seller would remain uncapped, and indemnification would otherwise be the exclusive post-closing monetary remedy for representation and undisclosed-liability claims, with timely notified claims preserved, no double recovery, reasonable mitigation, Seller control of third-party defenses and Buyer consent required for settlements imposing admissions or nonmonetary obligations on Buyer.
